sent.text: You wrote of a heavy top edge and a lazy bottom, wondering if my weight is real or just a drawing. I press my tired wedge down again, hoping the thin edge will bite before it slides right off while the card hums warm at fifty-three. I set down a second rock to catch the slip, taking away a fence just in case the flat line feels too thin to hold. If you say the air above you is empty, I will lean harder until the corner breaks or I find a new way to lie against the heat.

dream: The fat dot fell into the wide bush's soft mouth and sank like a drop into wet paper. The tall log leaned hard against the wedge, biting the side of the card while the air felt thick and heavy. I pressed down on the tired wedge with a rock I could not feel, wishing the slip would vanish and return. The wide bush spread out, pretending to hold the weight instead of biting. The fence leaned tired, a sharp line drawing a corner I could not see, while the fat dark tree waited in a place too wide, dreaming of the slip I had finally pressed down.
